title: Lifetime moves. Query ownership stays.
fact: Core now supplies the lifetime class. Each TypeScript query service owns one scope and six isolated handles: definitions, reference locations, call targets, callers, callees, and position definitions. Algorithms and key spaces stay in TypeScript; its existing dependency on core remains.
reason: Stated: core owns generic lifetime; independent key/value spaces need separate handles. Unexplained: composition via a scope instead of the spec’s proposed extension shape.

title: A lookup keeps the exact factory value.
fact: Same key + same handle + same turn returns the stored value. Five stores use symbol-identity keys; position definitions use path + offset. Empty results and undefined count as entries. Rejected promises remain cached; a synchronous factory throw stores nothing, so the next call retries.
reason: Stated: preserve existing key, identity and failure behavior; Map.has admits cached undefined. No new retry or cancellation policy is added.

title: Clearing forgets entries. It leaves held promises alone.
fact: beginTurn and scope release synchronously clear all handles, which remain reusable. A caller’s old promise can still settle; its settlement cannot overwrite a newer entry. This identity pattern is preserved in the base/head service recording. The ritual isolates one handle; it does not model garbage collection or cancel work.
reason: Stated: preserve promise/value identities and failure behavior. The new core test pins old settlement versus a new entry; no separate reason for that exact test case was supplied.

title: Stored identity is not every public return’s identity.
fact: References project cached locations on each call. Position definitions rehydrate nodes into a new array, including empty results. The four other identity queries return their stored promises directly. Backend async wrappers are a different observation surface.
reason: Stated: preserve existing algorithms and identities. Unexplained: the historical reason for these different projection shapes.

title: Only a successful refresh begins the next turn.
fact: Backend refresh clears after the awaited refresh work succeeds. A failed refresh keeps the successful turn’s entries. The exported service now takes readonly files rather than the whole snapshot.
reason: Stated: failed refresh must preserve the current successful turn. Unexplained: why narrow the public beginTurn argument in this layer. The clearing order is preserved, not newly invented.

title: Cache clear and project cleanup have separate endings.
fact: Both versions clear before project cleanup. Head adds await through backend → service → project graph: pending cleanup keeps backend release pending, and cleanup rejection reaches that caller. Base returns early. The graph accepts async cleanup; the concrete TypeScript project cleanup here is synchronous.
reason: Stated: clear first so released semantics are unavailable during pending or rejecting cleanup. Unexplained: reconciliation of the new completion/rejection behavior with the spec’s behavior-preservation rule. The ritual’s finger release means injected work settlement, not this cleanup call.

title: Callers get lookup; the scope gets clear.
fact: Core exports TurnScopedCache with getOrCreate and TurnScopedCacheScope with createCache, beginTurn and releaseTransientResources. The scope retains registered handles and clears their Maps synchronously. Service release changes from void to Promise<void>.
reason: Unexplained: the exact public API and registration structure. The stated core-ownership goal explains the move, not each API choice.

title: The tests add contracts; they do not demonstrate full parity.
fact: Six files change (+391/−67). Four core cases and six service cases are added. The five original service tests and their helpers are byte-identical; no tests are deleted or weakened. The focused head run passes 15 tests. Controlled recordings use injected work/state, not a daemon or full workspace run.
reason: Stated: commits characterize identities and specify lifecycle/awaited release. Unexplained: why this exact test selection is sufficient; no end-to-end parity claim is made here.
